whatItIs.text: Beef finely ground from the less tender cuts and trimmings; in the US a maximum of 30% fat by weight is allowed, and fat percentages are labelled so you can choose.

historyNote.text: Fat caps differ by country's food law: the US allows up to 30% fat by weight, France runs 5-20% (chains mostly 15%), and Germany's Tatar for steak tartare must stay under 5% — the same product, five times the legal range.

howToChoose.text: Choose packages that are bright red with clear date labels and the coldest stock in the case; leaner blends shrink less, fattier ones taste better in burgers and bolognese.

storage.text: Raw mince is the most perishable meat in the fridge — keep it cold on the bottom shelf and use within the rulebook's window, or freeze straight away.

foodSafetyRef.note: raw-mince storage and cooking rules live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Brown leftover mince with onion and tomato for a 15-minute ragu, or press into flatbreads with spices for quick kofta; cooked mince freezes well in flat packs that thaw fast.

substitutions.note: leaner and milder; cook with a little extra oil
for bolognese-style sauces; add umami (soy sauce, mushrooms)
